external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
external_entities.notes: The admin connects from wherever they happen to be; no location or trust zone is stated.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The CDN from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads and which provides the CDN bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server runs the CMS, serves the public site, accesses the MySQL database and pushes new assets to the CDN's bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The CMS running on the web server for the content site.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: The database containing pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I could not tell you whether the database is encrypted on disk."

data_stores.name: CDN bucket
data_stores.description: The bucket to which the web server pushes newly published assets.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.

data_flows.name: access site
data_flows.description: A reader accesses the public site served by the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: A reader fetches images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: keep content
data_flows.description: The CMS keeps pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated.
data_flows.data_description: newly published images, stylesheets and downloads

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

assumptions.assumption: The public site is reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it the public site and says readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The MySQL database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The database contains accounts and comments, which are personal or account-related records whose disclosure may harm users or the business.

assumptions.assumption: The CMS stores credentials or account credentials in the MySQL database.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains accounts; the controlled asset tag credentials represents account credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The CMS stores credentials or account credentials through its database interaction.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries accounts to the database, and accounts may contain credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The admin's database-maintenance flow carries credentials or account credentials.
assumptions.basis: The flow maintains a database stated to contain accounts, represented by the controlled asset tag credentials.
